SECTION 01 · THE PROBLEM
THE PROBLEM

Every Message Your Stack Sends Today Passes Through a Tollbooth

Picture a highway engineered for uninterrupted, high-speed travel — then imagine every car forced through the same manned tollbooth, one at a time, regardless of how many lanes the highway actually has. Three tollbooths are hiding in most latency-sensitive systems — and a fourth lane that has none at all.

Tollbooth 01 · OS Mutex Locks

The Boom Barrier

A guard steps out, checks a ticket, and raises the gate — one car at a time — even when nobody else actually wants the road right now.

Technical: a kernel-arbitrated mutex/futex parks the thread and wakes it via a context switch — hundreds of ns to µs per crossing, never the same twice.

COST: 100s ns–µs · NON-DETERMINISTIC
Tollbooth 02 · Cache False Sharing

The Single-Lane Bridge

Two cars in what should be independent lanes are funneled onto the same physical bridge deck — one driver braking makes the other brake too, though they were never meant to interact.

Technical: two unrelated variables sharing one 64-byte cache line force every core to invalidate and re-fetch the whole line on any write — silent contention, no lock in sight.

COST: SILENT THROUGHPUT LOSS · NO LOG
Tollbooth 03 · Python Serialization

The Border Customs Desk

Every vehicle is fully unpacked, inspected, stamped, and repacked before it may cross — even when nothing inside actually changed.

Technical: pickling, JSON encoding, and IPC copies pay a full serialize/deserialize tax at every process boundary — pure overhead, zero computation performed.

COST: FULL PICKLE/JSON TAX · EVERY MESSAGE

The Animus Express Lane

One dedicated lane, cache-isolated end to end — no barrier to stop for, no bridge deck to share, nothing to unpack.

30.3 ns · DETERMINISTIC · ZERO SYSCALLS

SECTION 02 · THE ARCHITECTURE
THE ARCHITECTURE

How One Message Crosses the Ring — Three Steps

A single-producer/single-consumer ring buffer, walked step by step: the write, the hardware isolation that makes it safe, and the zero-copy read on the other side.

1

Ingest — Producer Write

The producer writes payload bytes directly into a pre-allocated slot, then publishes the new head index with a release memory barrier — guaranteeing the consumer never sees a torn write.

2

Cache Isolation — 64B Boundary

alignas(64) pins head_ and tail_ to their own cache lines. Core 0 writing head_ never invalidates Core 1's copy of tail_ — no ping-pong, no false sharing.

3

Zero-Copy Consumer — Into Python

The consumer dereferences the same shared-memory pointer the producer wrote to — direct access, with no kernel mediation. Nothing is pickled, piped, or copied across the process boundary.

SECTION 02 · THE ARCHITECTURE
THE ARCHITECTURE

The Tick-to-Trade Decision Pipeline

The same ring-buffer discipline, applied end to end: a market-data tick or sensor packet enters one side, a decision leaves the other, in a fixed, measured budget.

1

Feed handler and parser run zero-allocation — parsing happens in place, on the wire buffer.

2

The lock-free channel is the same cache-isolated SPSC ring from the previous page — no locks between ingest and strategy.

3

Strategy logic polls rather than blocks; execution submits the instant a decision is made — no scheduler in the loop.

THE EVIDENCE

Four Orders of Magnitude, Not an Incremental Gain

Measured p50 latency to hand one message from a producer thread to a consumer thread — same host, same payload, same process — across four common transport mechanisms.

LOGARITHMIC SCALE — EACH GRIDLINE REPRESENTS A 10× CHANGE IN LATENCY

Baseline figures (TCP socket, named pipe, standard mutex queue) are representative order-of-magnitude values for common IPC/threading transports on modern commodity hardware, shown for scale — not a controlled head-to-head run on identical silicon. SECTION 04 · REAL-WORLD IMPACT
WHERE DETERMINISM IS NOT OPTIONAL

Three Domains Where a Missed Tick Has a Real Cost

Animus Core targets systems where p99 tail latency — not average throughput — decides the outcome.

Business Impact · Slippage Mitigation

Quantitative Finance Telemetry

Market-data feed handlers and order-routing telemetry where a single cache-line stall on the hot path is the difference between capturing a spread and reporting on one that already closed.

Business Impact · Zero-Jitter Control

Autonomous Robotics Control Loops

Sensor-to-actuator control loops that must complete a fixed-period cycle every time, not on average — jitter in the control loop is jitter in the physical motion of the machine.

Business Impact · Mission Assurance

Aerospace Sensor Fusion

Multi-sensor fusion pipelines (IMU, GPS, radar) merging readings from independent clocks into one coherent state estimate within a hard real-time budget, where a late tick is a safety event, not a support ticket.

SECTION 06 · ENGAGEMENT MODEL
ENGAGEMENT MODEL

Licensed as a Precompiled Engine, Integrated Like a Library

Precompiled Binary Licensing

Animus Core ships as a compiled C-ABI dynamic library (.dll / .so). Integrating partners receive the binary and headers, not the source tree — integration is a linker-level exercise, not a build-system project.

Zero-Dependency Python SDK

A ctypes-based Python 3.8+ wrapper calls directly into the native engine's exported C-ABI — zero-copy buffer handoff, no serialization layer, no third-party Python packages to audit or pin.

Deployment Posture

Runs fully on-premises or air-gapped. No telemetry, license phone-home, or external network dependency is required for the core engine to operate.

Registered Activity Classification

Filed under MCA NIC codes 62011 and 62013 — Computer Programming, Software Licensing & Technical Support.
